papers.title: Letter from Aunt Nell
lines: Dear Jo, I am sending the good teaspoons because you will only fight over them later.
The tin is under the pear tree at the back, where your Uncle Alf hid his pools winnings in 1971.
He swore it was a flowerpot. Do mind the roots.

trail.clue: Aunt Nell's tin lies in the ground where a pear tree stood. The nearest thing to remember it by is the open ground.

papers.title: Page from a silk ledger
lines: Received of Mr Barlow, eleven yards of figured twill, one yard short.
Entered as a loss. The yard was found in the cat's basket on Thursday.
Entered as a gain. The cat has not been charged rent.

papers.title: Bellringers' notice
lines: Practice is Thursday at half past seven. Tea is NOT provided, whatever Derek says.
New ringers welcome. You will be given a rope, a stern look and a biscuit, in that order.

papers.title: Toll receipt, 1824
lines: Received of Josiah Heap, for one boat of salt, forty hundredweight, passing the lock at Marbury.
Signed with a cross, as the toll keeper had mislaid his pen and his temper.

papers.title: Folded betting slip
lines: Chester Races, 2.30. Nelly's Pride, each way, two shillings.
On the back: 'If this comes in, I am buying the hat in the window at Browns. If it does not, I never saw this.'

papers.title: Note from a Land Girl
lines: Dear Mrs Pickford, I have left the eggs in the blue bowl and the ferret in the box.
Please do not confuse the two. I did once, and the less said the better.
Back for the milking at five. Yours, Edie.
